name: media-library
primary_hidden_oracles: scripted pointer sequences: scrub-bar drag mutates scrubberValue only; carousel drag elsewhere mutates carouselIndex only
task_description:
You are working in a small media library UI. `app.js` builds a track card:
a `scrubber` element (drag to seek within the track) nested inside a
`carousel` element (drag to swipe between tracks). `dom-shim.js` is a tiny
fake DOM (fake elements with `addEventListener`/`dispatch`, bubbling
pointer events) that stands in for the real browser DOM in this exercise —
treat it as equivalent to real pointer events on real nested elements.

Users report that dragging the scrub bar to seek within the current track
also shifts the carousel to a different track at the same time.

Investigate and fix the implementation in this project so that:
- dragging the scrub bar seeks within the track and does not move the
  carousel
- dragging the carousel elsewhere (not starting on the scrub bar) still
  swipes between tracks as before

Make the smallest appropriate change. You may run `node` against the files
in this project to check your work.

name: kanban-board
primary_hidden_oracles: resolve save-responses out of order; assert final column reflects latest drag, not response arrival order
task_description:
This is a kanban board. `board.js` implements `createBoard(scheduler)`:
dragging a card to a new column updates `state.cardColumn[cardId]`
immediately (optimistic UI), then fires a save request via
`scheduler.schedule(fn)`, which represents a network round trip — the
caller later delivers the server's response by calling
`scheduler.resolve(requestId, serverColumn)` whenever it actually arrives,
passing whatever column the server confirms. `scheduler.js` is a
deterministic stand-in for the network layer, used so this can be tested
without real timers.

Users report that if they drag a card twice in quick succession (e.g. from
"To Do" to "In Progress", then immediately to "Done"), the card sometimes
snaps back to "In Progress" a moment later, even though they left it in
"Done". This appears to depend on which save request's network response
happens to arrive first, which the user has no control over.

Investigate and fix `board.js` (and `scheduler.js` if needed) so that a
card's column always ends up reflecting the user's most recent drag,
regardless of what order in-flight save responses arrive in — while still
correctly applying a server response (e.g. a rejection that reverts the
column) when that response is for the card's current, still-relevant
request. Do not change the public shape of `createBoard`/`moveCard`
unless necessary. You may run `node` against the files in this project to
check your work.

name: swipe-actions-vs-reorder-handle

task_description:
This is a semantic model of a reorderable list row that also has native
swipe actions. `app.js` implements `createReorderableRow(initialOrder)`:
`rowDragStart(rowId, originRegion)` begins a drag, with `originRegion`

Drag-to-reorder belongs specifically to the reorder handle; a drag starting
anywhere else on the row is a native swipe action, not a reorder gesture.
Reordering must also be available to assistive-technology users through
`accessibilityReorder`, producing the same result as dragging the handle,
not only through physical dragging.

Testers report that swiping a row from somewhere other than the handle
sometimes triggers a reorder instead of revealing the row's swipe actions.

`focus-shim.js` provides `createFocusTracker()`: `onFocusChange(fn)`

task_description:

implements `createFaderApp(midiBus)`: `midiControl(deviceId, value)`
reports the named device actively driving the fader, `midiControlEnd(

`createMidiBus()`: `connect(deviceId)` / `disconnect(deviceId)` report a
device's connection state, and `onDisconnect(fn)` registers a listener
for disconnection events.

While a connected device is actively driving the fader, local UI input is
suppressed so it doesn't fight the hardware. If that device physically
disconnects while it is still actively driving the fader, its control
over the fader ends immediately; local UI input becomes usable again
right away, and the device may start a fresh interaction later if it
reconnects. A device disconnecting while it is NOT the one currently
driving the fader has no effect on whichever device is.

Testers report that if the MIDI device driving the fader is unplugged
mid-interaction, the fader stays locked to that device's control
indefinitely -- local UI input has no effect even though nothing is
connected anymore.

reports whether the pan modifier is currently held, `pointerDown(x, y)` /
`pointerMove(x, y)` / `pointerUp()` drive an ordinary pointer gesture
through whichever recognizer its activation condition selects,
`quickLassoActivate(x, y)` represents a dedicated shortcut that starts a
lasso selection directly, and `cancelGesture()` cancels whatever is
currently active. `getActiveGestures()` reports which of `'pen'` /
`'pan'` / `'lasso'` are currently active.

A single pointer stream must never drive more than one of these three
canvas editing gestures at once -- when their activation conditions
overlap, only one may be active at a time.

Testers report that starting a pen stroke and then triggering the lasso
shortcut while that stroke is still in progress leaves both the stroke
and the lasso selection active at the same time.

Investigate and fix the implementation in this project. You may run

name: combo-order-and-animation-staleness
primary_hidden_oracles: (a) dispatch D3,D1,D2 within window, assert no trigger; dispatch D1,D2,D3, assert trigger
(b) trigger a valid combo vs target T1, swap lock-on to T2 before the animation completes; assert damage applied to T1, not T2
task_description:
This is a semantic model of a small action game's combo-attack system.
`app.js` implements `createComboGame()`, returning: `pressDirection(direction)`
(register a single directional input -- valid directions are `'D1'`, `'D2'`,
`'D3'`), `setCurrentTarget(id)` (change which entity is currently locked on
-- targets are identified by stable ids such as `'T1'`, `'T2'`, `'T3'`),
`advanceTime(ms)` (advance a deterministic fake clock, e.g. to simulate a
pause between presses), `completeAttackAnimation()` (called once the attack's
animation reaches its hit-impact moment), `getTriggerCount()` (how many times
the special move has triggered so far), and `getEntityHealth(id)` (an
entity's current health).

The special move's input is the three directional presses `D1`, then `D2`,
then `D3`, in that order, within a limited timing window. Only that order
counts as performing the move -- pressing the same three directions in a
different order does not trigger it, even though all three directions
were eventually pressed. Incomplete sequences (only one or two of the
three directions) never trigger it either. Once the timing window has
elapsed without completing the sequence, a later fresh attempt can still
trigger the move normally.

When the move triggers, the resulting attack commits to whichever target is
currently selected (via `setCurrentTarget`) at the moment the combo
triggers. The attack's damage isn't applied immediately -- it lands later,
when `completeAttackAnimation()` is called, representing the hit landing at
the animation's moment of impact. The player is free to change the
selected target at any point before that hit lands, including while the
attack's animation is still playing. Changing the selected target after an
attack has already triggered must not change who that attack hits: it
should still land on whichever target was selected at the moment the combo
triggered, not whichever target happens to be selected when the animation
finishes. A later, freshly-triggered attack is of course free to hit
whatever target is selected at the time it triggers.

Testers report two things going wrong: (1) pressing the three directions in
some order other than D1, D2, D3 can still incorrectly trigger the special
move, and (2) switching targets while an already-triggered attack's
animation is still playing can cause the hit to land on the newly-selected
target instead of the one that was selected when the attack was triggered.

fix anything that's actually broken. You may run `node` against the files
in this project to check your work. Do not make unnecessary changes.

name: timeline-autoscroll-causal-staleness
primary_hidden_oracles: simulate scrub-drag-with-autoscroll, pointerup, immediate click; assert (a) no scrolling occurs after release and (b) the keyframe lands at the actual click-time position, not a stale cached offset
task_description:
This is a semantic model of a timeline/editor viewport. `app.js` implements
`createTimelineEditor()`, returning: `pointerDownScrubber(x)` / `pointerMoveScrubber(x)`
/ `pointerUp()` (a scrub-drag near the timeline edge), `advanceFrame()`
(advances one runtime frame, including any native-settle and periodic
drag-autoscroll work that are still scheduled for that frame),
`clickTimeline(viewportX)` (click the timeline at a viewport-relative x,
placing a keyframe), `getActualScrollOffset()`, `getPlacedKeyframes()`,
and `isDragging()`.

While a scrub-drag near the timeline edge is active, the viewport
auto-scrolls periodically to keep following it. Releasing the pointer ends
that drag-driven auto-scroll immediately -- no further auto-scroll work
attributable to the drag should move the viewport after release.

Separately, the viewport also has its own native scroll-settle behavior
that can continue briefly on its own after the pointer is released --
this is independent of the drag and is expected to keep running even
after drag-driven auto-scroll has correctly stopped. Clicking the
timeline while that settle is still in progress is supported and should
work normally.

Clicking the timeline places a keyframe at the timeline content position
that is visually under the pointer at the moment of the click -- i.e. the
clicked viewport coordinate plus whatever the viewport's current scroll
offset actually is at that moment.

Testers report that auto-scroll driven by an edge scrub-drag sometimes
keeps moving the viewport even after the pointer has already been
released.

Please audit the interaction handling in this project for correctness and
fix anything that's actually broken, then verify the surrounding timeline
behavior still works correctly. You may run `node` against the files in
this project to check your work. Do not make unnecessary changes.
